name: Mail
description: Read and send email from Antimatter, over IMAP and SMTP.

settings_schema.header: Users connect their own mailbox over IMAP (reading) and SMTP (sending), with a password or by signing in with Google or Microsoft once set up below. Passwords and sign-ins are stored encrypted; users should use app passwords where their provider offers them.

settings.display_name: Allow mail servers on private networks
settings.help_text: When true, users can connect to mail servers on loopback, private and link-local addresses, such as a mail server on your internal network. Leave it off unless your mail server is on such a network: it would also let users reach the other internal services of the network this server runs in.
When true, users can connect to mail servers without TLS. Their passwords and mail then cross the network unencrypted.
How often the inbox of each online user is checked for new mail, to update their unread count.
Messages larger than this can't be opened in Antimatter.

Lets users connect a Gmail or Google Workspace mailbox by signing in with Google, rather than with an app password. Create an OAuth client of type "Web application" in the Google Cloud console, with the redirect URI <Site URL>/plugins/com.antimatterchat.mail/oauth/callback, and enable the Gmail API. See the plugin's README.
The secret of the Google OAuth client.

Lets users connect an Outlook.com or Microsoft 365 mailbox by signing in with Microsoft. Register an application in Microsoft Entra ID with the Web redirect URI <Site URL>/plugins/com.antimatterchat.mail/oauth/callback and the delegated permissions IMAP.AccessAsUser.All and SMTP.Send. See the plugin's README.
A client secret of the Microsoft application.

Who can sign in with Microsoft: "common" for any work, school or personal account, "organizations" for work and school accounts, "consumers" for personal accounts, or your tenant ID or domain for your organization only.
